newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission urges joint action on energy problems.
newsitem.headline: Commission urges joint action on energy problems.

text.p: The European Commission called on Wednesday for a concerted effort to tackle the European Union's soaring dependence on non-EU energy supplies, ensure competitive energy prices and protect the environment.

By the year 2020, the EU's reliance on external sources of natural gas, coal and oil could rise from 50 percent to as much as 70, 80 and 90 percent respectively, the Commission said in a strategy paper.
At the same time, the EU member states are under pressure to cut electricity and gas prices, and to reduce the damage the energy sector does to the environment.

"Faced with these challenges, the member states and the EU have developed a range of measures. However, it has to be noted that these actions often lack transparency, targeting and coordination," the Commission said.

It suggested these efforts would be more effective if they were targeted more accurately at four specific areas -- improving security of supply, integrating Europe's national energy markets, encouraging sustainable development and promoting energy research and development.

As the starting point for creating a clear, coherent EU energy policy, the Commission document presents for the first time a complete picture of all the energy-related initiatives being carried out in the four priority areas.

These range from energy saving schemes and plans to develop trans-European energy networks, to promoting renewable resources, research nuclear safety, and cooperation schemes with energy-rich countries in Eastern Europe and North Africa.

With this information to hand, plus details of all the possible sources of financing, EU energy ministers will be in a better position to adopt a cost-efficient strategy which avoids duplication and loopholes, the Commission said.
